advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) because its methods operate on two distinct clusters of attributes: one cluster uses `_width` for formatting (`title`, `describe_customer`), while the other cluster uses `_repository` and `_mailer` for data retrieval and communication (`order_count`, `mail_summary`). Additionally, `describe_customer` demonstrates feature envy by accessing four attributes of the `Customer` object rather than its own state, suggesting a responsibility mismatch.

suggestions.title: Extract formatting logic to a dedicated Formatter class
suggestions.sketch: Create a `ReportFormatter` class that holds `_width` and contains `title()` and `describe_customer()`. `ReportView` would then delegate these calls to the formatter. This separates the presentation concern (width, string manipulation) from the data access concern (repository, mailer), reducing the connected components in the method-attribute graph of `ReportView`.

suggestions.title: Move customer description logic to Customer or a CustomerPresenter
suggestions.sketch: The method `describe_customer` accesses `customer.customer_id()`, `customer.name()`, `customer.email()`, and `customer.tier()`. This is feature envy. Move this logic to the `Customer` class (e.g., `customer.to_report_string(width)`) or a dedicated `CustomerPresenter`. This reduces the dependency of `ReportView` on the internal structure of `Customer` and improves cohesion by placing the logic where the data resides.

advices.risk_notes: Extracting the formatter increases the number of classes in the system (DCC up) and may introduce indirection. Moving logic to `Customer` requires ensuring that `Customer` does not become a god object if other similar presentation logic is added. The current `ReportView` is small (NOM=4), so over-engineering should be avoided; these changes are primarily for clarity and cohesion rather than performance.
